key_insight: FeTS++ expands federated medical imaging benchmarking by adding a classification task and moving to NVFlare, while evaluating methods on a larger, more diverse multi-institutional brain tumor dataset.
clinical_relevance: This challenge helps test whether privacy-preserving, cross-site AI can improve tumor segmentation and tumor-type classification across diverse real-world hospitals.
method: Federated learning keeps site data local while training shared models across institutions.
Task 1 evaluates aggregation strategies for segmentation models.
Task 2 evaluates federated glioma-vs-meningioma classification under site-confounded labels.
evidence_signal: The challenge uses clinically acquired multi-parametric MRI from the BraTS 2025 Lighthouse cohort spanning gliomas and meningiomas across institutions in North America, Europe, Asia, and Africa, and ranks methods by utility plus an efficiency-aware score.
watch_item: Because tumor label is strongly confounded with institution/site of origin, classification performance may reflect site signals as much as biology unless carefully controlled.
paper_title: The Federated Tumor Segmentation and Classification (FeTS++) Challenge
